Definition

What Is WordPress Website Error Repair?

WordPress website error repair is the process of finding the technical cause of a WordPress failure — such as a PHP fatal error, a plugin or theme conflict, a failed update, a database error, a server limit or a malware infection — and fixing that cause so the website works normally again, without rebuilding the site or losing content.

A broken WordPress site is rarely a mystery. Every critical error, white screen, 500 error or collapsed layout comes from something specific: a plugin calling a function your PHP version no longer supports, a memory limit reached during a page load, a damaged table in the database, a bad rule in .htaccess, or code injected by an attacker. Our job is to find that exact point of failure, fix it properly and confirm the whole website works again — not only the page you noticed first.

  • Critical errors and PHP fatal errors
  • White Screen of Death (WSoD)
  • Error establishing a database connection
  • 500, 502 and 503 server errors
  • Plugin and theme conflicts after updates
  • Login loops, 403 Forbidden and admin lockouts
  • Broken Elementor, Divi and page builder layouts
  • Hacked sites, spam redirects and malware warnings
  • Slow WordPress sites and poor Core Web Vitals
  • Broken contact forms, email and WooCommerce checkout

If your website worked yesterday, it can usually be repaired today — no rebuild required.

Fix Website Issues has repaired 1,000+ websites since 2013. Repairs are done by our own technicians, and you pay only after the work is done.

Warning Signs

Signs Your WordPress Website Needs Repair

Some WordPress problems appear the moment an update finishes. Others build slowly until visitors leave or forms stop sending. If you see any of these, your website needs a technical review:

  • “There has been a critical error on this website”
  • Blank white screen on the site or in wp-admin
  • “Error establishing a database connection”
  • 500, 502, 503 or 504 server errors
  • Website broke after a WordPress, plugin or PHP update
  • Admin login keeps returning to the login page
  • Pages load without styling or the layout has collapsed
  • The Elementor or Divi editor will not load
  • Contact forms stop sending emails
  • Visitors are redirected to spam or casino sites
  • Google shows “This site may be hacked” or a red warning
  • The website is suddenly very slow or times out

Repeatedly deactivating plugins, switching themes or restoring random backups can make the problem harder to trace — and can erase recent orders, leads and posts.

If your website takes payments, bookings or patient and client enquiries, call us before making changes yourself.

Common Errors We Fix

WordPress Errors We Diagnose and Repair

Each problem has a different cause and a different fix. Here is what each error usually means and how we repair it.

Critical & PHP Fatal Errors

“There has been a critical error on this website” usually means a plugin or theme threw a fatal PHP error, often after an update. We trace it to the exact file and line, fix or replace the failing code, and restore compatibility with your PHP version.

White Screen of Death

A blank screen with no message usually points to memory exhaustion or a silent fatal error. We check the server and PHP error logs, correct memory limits, and repair the theme, plugin or core files causing the crash.

Database Connection Errors

When WordPress cannot reach MySQL or MariaDB, the whole site goes down. We verify the database service, check the credentials and host in wp-config.php, and repair corrupted tables.

500, 502 & 503 Server Errors

Server errors come from a bad .htaccess rule, PHP timeouts, exhausted resources or a hosting configuration problem. We read the logs, correct the configuration and work with your host when a server-side change is needed.

Plugin & Theme Conflicts

Two plugins loading the same library, or a theme overriding code that changed in an update, can break features site-wide. We isolate the conflict safely, then fix, replace or reconfigure the component — not just switch it off.

Failed Updates & PHP Upgrades

Interrupted core updates leave a site stuck in maintenance mode or half-updated, and PHP 8.x upgrades expose outdated code. We complete or roll back the update and patch incompatible code so you can keep updating safely.

Login Loops, 403 & Lockouts

Correct passwords that loop back to the login page, 403 Forbidden screens or a lost admin account. We fix site URL and cookie settings, security keys, firewall blocks and user roles, and restore your administrator access.

Broken Layouts & Page Builders

Pages without styling, collapsed grids, or an Elementor or Divi editor that will not open. We fix mixed-content and REST API problems, regenerate CSS files and clear stale server and CDN caches.

Hacked Sites & Spam Redirects

Redirects to spam sites, unknown admin users or Google security warnings. We compare files against clean originals, remove backdoors and injected code, clean the database and harden the site.

Slow WordPress Websites

Heavy plugins, oversized images, missing caching or a bloated database can make WordPress slow. We measure what is actually slowing the site and fix it, instead of stacking more optimization plugins.

Forms & Email Not Sending

Contact forms that look fine but never deliver. We check form settings, SMTP and email authentication so enquiries reach your inbox again, then test every form on the site.

WooCommerce & Checkout Errors

Checkout failures, payment gateway errors or carts that empty after an update. We troubleshoot WooCommerce carefully so live orders and customer data stay protected.

Repair, Not Rebuild

Why Trial-and-Error Troubleshooting Makes WordPress Problems Worse

When a website crashes, the usual reaction is to disable every plugin, switch themes, reinstall WordPress or restore whatever backup the host has. Each of these can hide the real cause — or create new problems:

  • Error logs overwritten before the cause is found
  • Plugin settings lost when plugins are deleted
  • Recent orders, leads and posts erased by an old backup
  • Page builder layouts broken by switching themes
  • Malware left behind because only the symptom was removed
  • New conflicts from installing more “fix” plugins

If a website worked yesterday, it can almost always be repaired today without starting over. A rebuild costs far more, takes weeks and can put the rankings you have already earned at risk.

Straight Answers

Why Did My WordPress Website Break After an Update?

Short answer

Why did my WordPress website break after an update?

Most update crashes happen because a plugin, theme or custom code is not compatible with the new version of WordPress, another plugin, or the PHP version on your server. The update itself usually works — the code that depends on it fails. The fix is to identify the incompatible component from the error log, then update, patch or replace it so the website runs on current, secure versions instead of being frozen on old ones.

Rolling back the update fixes the symptom for today. Fixing the incompatible code fixes it for good.

Quick Answers

WordPress Errors Explained in Plain English

Short, direct answers to the questions business owners ask most when their WordPress website stops working.

What does “There has been a critical error” mean?

WordPress caught a fatal PHP error and stopped loading the page to protect the site. The cause is almost always a specific plugin, theme or custom code file, which the error log identifies.

What causes the White Screen of Death?

Usually PHP memory exhaustion or a fatal error with error display turned off. The server and PHP error logs show which file failed and why.

What causes a database connection error?

Wrong database credentials in wp-config.php, a database server that is down or overloaded, or corrupted database tables.

Can a WordPress site be fixed without losing content?

Yes. Posts, pages, media and orders live in the database and uploads folder. We back up both before any repair and fix only the component that failed.

Is it safe to update plugins on a broken site?

Not until the cause is known. Updating blindly can trigger new conflicts. We identify the failing component first, then update in a controlled order.

Why does my site work for me but not for visitors?

Caching. Logged-in users often bypass the cache while visitors see an old or broken copy. Server, plugin and CDN caches must be cleared after the real fix.

When should I call for help instead of fixing it myself?

When the site handles sales, bookings or enquiries, when you are locked out of wp-admin, when Google shows a security warning, or when a fix you tried made things worse.

WordPress Error Repair FAQs

Straight answers about fixing critical errors, white screens, database errors, hacked sites and broken WordPress websites.
1. How quickly can you fix a broken WordPress website?

Most common WordPress errors — including critical errors, the White Screen of Death, database connection errors and single plugin conflicts — are fixed within 2–4 hours. Complex multi-plugin conflicts, hosting problems or deep malware infections can take longer, and we tell you the expected time before we start.

2. How much does WordPress error repair cost?

WordPress fixes start at $50 and hacked website repair is $200. The final price depends on what is broken. We confirm the cause and the cost on a free live error check before any work begins.

3. Do I have to pay a deposit?

No. There is no upfront deposit. We diagnose and fix the problem, test the website, and you review it. You pay only after the work is done.

4. Will repairing my website delete my content, orders or leads?

No. We back up your files, uploads and database before making any change, and we fix only the component that failed. For live WooCommerce stores and lead forms, risky changes are tested on staging first so orders and submissions stay protected.

5. What does “There has been a critical error on this website” mean?

It means WordPress caught a fatal PHP error and stopped loading to protect the site. The cause is usually a plugin, theme or custom code that is incompatible with your WordPress or PHP version. We find the exact file in the error log and fix it.

6. Why did my WordPress website break after an update?

Most update crashes happen because a plugin, theme or custom code is not compatible with the new version of WordPress, another plugin or your server’s PHP version. We identify the incompatible component and update, patch or replace it so you can keep updating safely.

7. Can you fix my site if I am locked out of wp-admin or my developer is unavailable?

Yes. With access to your hosting account (cPanel, Plesk or your host’s dashboard) or SFTP, we can restore administrator access, fix login loops and 403 errors, and recover the website even if your previous developer cannot be reached.

8. Can you fix a hacked WordPress website?

Yes. We remove malware, backdoors, spam redirects and unknown admin users, clean the database, harden the website and help request removal of Google security warnings. Hacked website repair is $200.

9. Do you repair Elementor, Divi and WooCommerce websites?

Yes. We repair broken Elementor and Divi layouts, editors that will not load, and WooCommerce checkout, payment and cart errors, along with general WordPress plugin and theme problems.

10. Do you provide WordPress repair across the United States?

Yes. We are based in Houston, Texas and repair WordPress websites for businesses in all 50 states, with 24/7 support by phone or text at 832-266-7209.

11. Do you offer support after the fix?

Yes. After a repair we can provide guidance and optional ongoing website maintenance, starting from $300/month, to keep WordPress, plugins and security up to date.
